findings.description: Flagged dynamic regex `re.findall("{(.*?)}", path)` is a static literal with a lazy quantifier bounded by literal braces - no catastrophic backtracking, no ReDoS.
findings.code_snippet:
def get_path_param_names(path: str) -> Set[str]:
    return set(re.findall("{(.*?)}", path))
findings.reasoning: The query (py/regex-survey) flags any regex whose pattern is a string literal, flagging it as 'potentially dynamic'. Here the pattern is a hardcoded constant `"{(.*?)}"` with zero user influence over pattern construction, so regex injection is impossible. For ReDoS (CWE-1333): the pattern contains a single lazy group `(.*?)` delimited by two distinct literal characters `{` and `}`. There are no nested or overlapping quantifiers and no ambiguous alternation, so matching is effectively linear in input length. Even with an adversarial, very long `path` value containing many `{` characters and no closing brace, the engine advances one character at a time per start position - O(n) per literal `{`, and the whole `findall` remains polynomial worst case at worst for typical Python `re` scanning, not exponential. No exponential blowup is possible since each attempt fails as soon as the fixed `}` terminator cannot be found and the lazy group has no other partition choices to explore. Therefore no ReDoS.
